2026-07-16 China

China Day 6

Today was second and final test! After answering all of our student's questions during the Q&A portion of the test, we moved to the hotel where the Deputy Leaders are staying which is much closer to the students. My room is quite fancy. The bathroom is bigger than the living room in our appartment, lol.

After lunch, we went to see the students at Shanghai High School (where they are staying). This high school is one of the top high schools in China with high performing students in all areas you could possibly think of.

They have a forest in the middle of the high school!

Tests are now done and with that I hope the students just worry about having fun for the rest of the IMO. With that in mind, we wanted to make sure they took time to do some fun activities and they were really hoping to go to Oriental Peart TV Tower. There are regulations to follow for the students to get out of the school when it's not for a scheduled trip. After signing a bunch of waivers, and almost an hour of figuring out how to get taxis, we were headed to the Tower.

Oriental Pearl Tower

The view was great. I'm not sure my photos actually show it, but I really like how the lake goes through the city. I was shocked at how many locals were at this attractions. I had read online that, unlike other countries, tourist attractions are actually quite common for locals too, and this really showed that for me.

Taxis

Before coming to China, Rachel and I did some research on best ways to pay for stuff and how to order a cab. We setup Alipay and Wechat for this. Some of the kids that came had done so as well. Unfortunately, for most people additionally setup still require getting SMS verification codes that were no longer possible to get here. Thankfully my setup was (initially fine), so I was able to get a cab on our way to the Tower. However, my account was flagged as suspicious and could no longer do it afterwards without doing a full in-person verification of my account. On our way back we had to get taxis on the street that clearly wanted to scam us by charging 3-4x the regular price. Finally we had to accept a 30% higher rate since we needed to get the kids back to the dorms before curfew. When haggling over the price with the driver, we were using a translator app and I said "This ride is X% higher than what DiDi is showing", to what he replied "But you can't get that right now, can you?" which I thought was hilarious and eventually agreed on something more reasonable.
